To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have obtained the deepest image to date of a hot Jupiter at 150 MHz and have obtained the most stringent upper limit yet achieved for the quiescent and rotational modulation of the radio emission of a hot Jupiter.

the 150 MHz upper limit for τ Boo b is 1.2mJy and the upper limit for the radio emission from a 10 G magnetic field is 1.3 mJy, which is a factor of 10 higher than the predicted flux density of 0.1 mJy.
we have obtained the deepest image yet published at 150 MHz of the hot Jupiter tau Bootis b and have placed the most stringent upper limit yet on its radio flux density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic field in the atmosphere of the hot Jupiter, τ Bootis b.
the study of the radio emission of the hot Jupiter, τ Boötis b (τ Boo b).
the detection and study of radio emission from exoplanetary systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radio emission is not detected at the 3σ level.
we have not yet detected the radio emission from τ Bootis b and that the next generation of telescopes will be required for its detection.
the hot Jupiter τ Boo b has not yet been detected in radio emission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hot Jupiter τ Boötis b is not detected at 150 MHz and the upper limits we have derived are the lowest yet achieved for a hot Jupiter.
τ Bootis b has not been detected as an active radio source.

τ Bootis b remains the most promising candidate for detection of low-frequency radio emission from hot Jupiters, and that the detection of such emission would provide a new probe of the magnetic field strength of the planet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of radio emission from τ Bootis b will be challenging and will likely require a dedicated radio telescope array such as LOFAR.
hot Jupiters are not a likely population of radio sources at these frequencies.
hot Jupiters are unlikely sources of low-frequency radio emission at flux density levels detectable by the SKA.
